author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell and his wife Laura discuss the idea that modern systems are ultimately designed for control, built in a way that will parasitically consume you if you let it, even when that same culture occasionally produces something genuinely good, a beautiful film, a great meal, a piece of music. They argue those moments of beauty are still just a byproduct, not the system's real function. The conversation turns to James's instruction to submit to God and resist the devil, and lands on a striking reframe, that returning to faith isn't converting to something new at all, it's returning to a natural state that existed before the fall, back in Eden. A reflective, thought provoking watch on what it really means to come home.

title: What is culture actually designed to do?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell and his wife Laura dig into why rest feels so difficult to accept, even when it's exactly what's needed, and land on a surprising answer, it isn't really about the workload, it's about control. They discuss the fear that stopping means falling further behind, and reference the book Rest by Alex Soojung Kim Pang, which argues that real rest has to be taken deliberately and protected from a world intent on stealing it. Russell shares a small practical shift, doing the demanding tasks early in the day so the rest of it can move slower and gentler. A grounded conversation for anyone who struggles to actually stop, even when they know they need to.
